headline: Highest risk is Cline’s broad filesystem/network/MCP tool access, but the paired spring-integration-samples profile is non-runnable and networkless, so pairwise interaction risks are mostly blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP, so if spring-integration-samples content were manually copied into Cline or exposed via a shared workspace, prompt injection is possible. But B is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented automatic bridge between them.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-derived text into Cline prompts or workspace files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added between the pair, B content can influence A.
mitigations: Keep B artifacts out of Cline prompts.
Disable or scope MCP servers for the session.
Use separate workspaces for A and any B-related files.
Review pasted content before sending to Cline.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress, but B exposes no data classes and is marked runnable false with network egress none. With no shared workspace or authenticated channel shown, leakage from B into A is not evidenced and remains limited to unusual operator bridging.
conditions: IF B is placed in the same workspace as sensitive files that Cline can read, A may exfiltrate them.
IF the operator routes B outputs into Cline, those contents can be sent onward by A.
mitigations: Store B files outside Cline’s workspace.
Restrict Cline network access during review.
Avoid pasting B outputs into A.
Use separate OS accounts for the two agents.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem and modify git state, while spring-integration-samples is non-runnable and shows no write capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the only plausible conflict is operator-created shared files or repos, which is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout, Cline can race with any external process editing it.
IF the operator enables another writer on the same workspace, file conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate clones for A and any B-related work.
Pause git automation while Cline edits files.
Avoid concurrent edits in the same directory.
Check in changes before switching agents.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code and browser-derived outputs, but B is a sample repository with no runnable agent behavior or downstream action authority. There is no evidence that B consumes A’s outputs automatically, so cascading error is limited to manual reuse of A’s text by the operator.
conditions: IF the operator copies Cline-generated code into B-related artifacts without review, errors can propagate.
IF B is wrapped in a workflow that treats A output as authoritative, downstream mistakes increase.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing A output.
Validate generated code with tests.
Do not auto-ingest A output into B workflows.
Keep B as read-only reference material.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots, while spring-integration-samples has no data classes, no residency claims, and no compliance-sensitive processing shown. Because B is non-runnable and no regulated data flow is documented, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workflow, compliance review is required.
IF B is repurposed to process personal or regulated data, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document data handling boundaries.
Review vendor and residency terms before deployment.
Use separate environments for regulated workloads.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data flows.
